title: Tiergarten Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Tiergarten is 210 hectares of free, open park in the middle of Berlin, and it never closes.** It began in 1527 as a royal hunting ground and was redesigned into the park you see today by Peter Joseph Lenné between 1833 and 1838.

**Almost every tree in the park was planted after 1949.** Coal shortages after WWII meant Berliners cut most of the park down for firewood; only about 700 of over 200,000 trees survived. Around 250,000 replacement trees arrived as donations over the following decade.

**The main landmarks are the Victory Column, the Soviet War Memorial and Bellevue Palace.** The Soviet War Memorial commemorates 80,000 Soviet soldiers and was built within months of the war ending in 1945. Bellevue Palace is the German President's official residence and has no public entry.
**The quieter western half has the Englischer Garten, the lion-guarded Löwenbrücke, and the Neuer See**, where you can rent a rowboat for about 10 EUR an hour in season.

**Use the loop planner below to match your visit to the time you actually have.** There is no single entrance; Brandenburger Tor, Bellevue, Tiergarten and Zoologischer Garten stations all drop you at a different corner of the park.
**Tiergarten is not on my own walking tour route**, which stays in the medieval core near Alexanderplatz. Treat it as a separate slower half-day rather than a rushed add-on.
